text: Subsidies, taxes, and regulations can all lead to power plants that pollute less by switching away from coal. <break time="0.8s" /> In all cases, profits can be higher from making the transition, even taking the related costs into account. <break time="0.8s" /> The power plants prefer subsidies over regulations or taxes. <break time="0.8s" /> The reason is obvious. <break time="0.8s" /> They prefer to receive money from the government rather than pay the costs themselves. <break time="0.8s" /> But the expansion of their opportunity set through subsidies has to be matched by the contraction of the opportunity set of others. <break time="0.8s" /> The electricity companies freedom is increased at the expense of the ordinary individual, who must suffer from increased taxation to pay for the subsidy. <break time="0.8s" /> Moreover, from the perspective of pure efficiency, the subsidy distorts the economy because the electricity company is not facing the full costs of what it does, even if it is successful in limiting emissions. <break time="0.8s" /> Indeed, electricity prices may end up lower than they should be and electricity consumption higher, which will worsen global warming, even though the emissions per unit of electricity have been reduced.
